text:
nisha: quick heads-up — tried publishing a dual build (cjs + esm) for the js sdk and hit two kinds of breakage in the wild: edge runtimes throwing because of Node-only APIs, and some consumers seeing auth retry loops in cjs consumers only.

sam: can you paste the package.json exports you used?

nisha: sure — minimal: 
```json
"exports": {".": {"import": "./dist/esm/index.js", "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js"}},
"main": "dist/cjs/index.js",
"module": "dist/esm/index.js",
"types": "dist/index.d.ts"
```

maria: that looks normal. what edge errors are you seeing? stack traces?

nisha: Cloudflare workers + Vercel edge throw: "ReferenceError: Buffer is not defined" from our auth nonce generation path (we were doing Buffer.from(randomBytes)). Also a couple of top-level imports use "crypto.randomFillSync" which isn't available.

evan: ohhh — classic. Node vs Web Crypto differences. for edge we should ship an "edge" build that uses globalThis.crypto. Or guard the calls.

sam: why auth retries are different in CJS though?

nisha: looks like our retry wrapper pulls in a small internal platform detection that prefers node-fetch in cjs path; node-fetch re-creates Request/Response shapes and our retry logic checks instanceof Response which fails across realms so it keeps retrying.

maria: ugh. instanceof issues. We saw that before with cross-bundle Response objects. simpler to make retry logic duck-type (status, headers, json method) instead of instanceof.

evan: agree. also: beware of conditional exports + types. Typescript consumers sometimes resolve types to the wrong file when we have separate dist/esm and dist/cjs d.ts files. tsserver sometimes picks the cjs d.ts for an import('pkg').default in ESM projects.

sam: any recommended package.json layout to reduce surprises?

maria: we've had good luck with: 
```json
"exports": {".": {"types": "./dist/index.d.ts","import": "./dist/esm/index.js","require": "./dist/cjs/index.js","edge": "./dist/edge/index.js"}},
"types": "./dist/index.d.ts"
```
Note: "types" inside export conditions is ignored by older Node but many tools will pick the top-level types. Keep a single entrypoint d.ts that re-exports platform-specific types.

evan: Another option is a tiny runtime shim: cjs wrapper that re-exports esm default to avoid interop mismatches. e.g. dist/cjs/index.js: 
```js
module.exports = require('../esm/index.js').default || require('../esm/index.js');
```
That helps older consumers that expect module.exports.default vs module.exports.

nisha: we're also hitting top-level await problems in the esm build (some bundlers choke). solution: avoid top-level await in the entry — move async init behind createClient() factory.

sam: good call. coming back to edge: do we want to publish a separate "edge" entrypoint in exports? like "edge": "./dist/edge/index.js" so bundlers/platforms can pick it?

maria: yes + document it in changelog. but ensure the edge build is pure ESM and uses Web Crypto/fetch only. Include a small readme: "edge build uses globalThis.fetch and web-crypto; node build uses node-crypto; choose by import or let bundler pick."

release-bot: canary 0.12.3-edge published with dist/edge and dist/esm artifacts :thumbsup:

evan: follow-ups — 1) patch retry duck-typing ASAP, 2) add edge build with crypto shims, 3) avoid top-level await in entry, 4) create a single canonical d.ts that re-exports platform-specific types. I can open PRs for 1 and 3.

nisha: thanks. I'll draft PR for edge build and add tests on Cloudflare worker runner. also will add a small snippet to README about "if you get Buffer is not defined, use the edge import or polyfill globalThis.Buffer".

maria: for publish playbook — let's add a checklist item: smoke test installs in node ESM, node CJS, vite+vite-ssr, cloudflare worker, bun. tiny matrix but saves us headaches.

sam: agreed. i'll add a checklist item and a CI job that runs quick smoke tests.

nisha: cool — thanks y'all. I'll link PRs here when ready. :pray:
